Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, a gas giant so massive
that its mass is roughly two and a half times that of all the other
planets combined. Jupiter has dozens of known moons, including the four
large Galilean moons discovered by Galileo Galilei in 1610: Io, Europa,
Ganymede, and Callisto. Its most famous feature is the Great Red Spot, a
gigantic storm larger than Earth that has raged for centuries.

Because Jupiter is a gas giant, it has no solid surface. Beneath its thick
atmosphere of hydrogen and helium, pressure and temperature increase until
hydrogen behaves like a metal, which is thought to generate Jupiter's
powerful magnetic field.
